posts.name: Dandolo
posts.cooked:
Ironic:

Why those six?  No love for the Naturalst, the Scholar, or Chrono-Ranger?

 

Lots of love for all 3 of those heroes plus Sky-Scraper, Omnitron-X, the Southwest Sentinels and Parse (my favorite hero.)  I picked these 6 because:

  1. Ra is the only hero from the base game with only 1 promo, he is central to the OblivAeon story and Christopher answered to a question in the Q&A about Ra promo in the Q&A with " Perhaps. If you're good."

  2. The Dark Watch Heroes because giving each of them a promo would mean each hero from Infernal Relics or earlier would have 2. Setback's only current promo was released before his deck and I'm guessing Christopher might want to make a new one now that he has the deck to go with. Plus Setback's mechanic is so unique and awesome if I were a game designer I'd want to find a fun way to change his game up (same holds true for NightMist and Mr. Fixer).

  3. That leaves KNYFE which is basicly a shot in the dark. My reasoning was she's the hero whose goal was the most closely tied to stopping OblivAeon (other than Lifeline but he's 1. new and 2. already getting a promo with this expansion.

  4. The heroes you listed all got promo's with Villains. Chrono's sparked lots of debate and its pretty hard to come up with another idea for what a Nataralist power could be be thats not similar to his existing 2.

 

Of course, I would never have guessed additional Prime Wardens promos or a Heroic Akash'bhuta so psychic powers aside I don't really put too much stock in my own insites into the mad genius that is Christopher.

edit: Also I would love those "Be The Gate" Heroes but there are 7 of them which makes them seem less likely to me.

posts.name: aawood
posts.cooked:
BlueHairedMeerkat:

I don't see the last thing ever added to Sentinels being cards you swap in and out of a deck, given that's never been done before…

That's kinda why I think it's plausible; SotM has a history of finding new ways to play with the format and introducing new concepts. A few ideas off the top of my head (please correct me if I'm wrong about when these were introduced, but fairly sure they all came in after the base game):

  • Ambuscade added face-up trap cards.
  • The Ennead added villains with multiple character cards.
  • The Sentinels added Heroes with multiple character cards.
  • Vengeance added a whole playstyle.
  • Villains added a bunch of stuff, which I'll totally get around to trying out one day.
  • Setback added their own token pool.
  • The Tomb of Anubis added the prizes to give players extra abilities from outside their deck.
  • Khagraa added a whole extra deck outside the usual Environments/Heroes/Villains types. (I don't know if the Title Deck technically counts as a villain deck, but still, you get the point.)
  • Spite added the Safehouse and Drugs.
  • Sky Scraper added swapping character cards.
  • Unity added a hero based around cards she couldn't directly play.
  • Chrono-Ranger and Captain Cosmic both added Heroes based primarily around playing cards into other areas (bounties for CR, constructs for CC).
  • The Temple of Zhu Long added the idea of an environment hiding cards in your deck.
  • Celestrial Tribunal added bringing in cards from the box to the current game.
  • Completionist Guise in the box looks like adding specialist tokens, along with whatever the heck they're used for.
  • As for Oblivaeon itself, it's already giving us a third (final?) playstyle, and the first full new decks for existing heroes (Void Guard).
  • Oh, and going way back; America's Newest Legacy gave us alternate character cards for decks.
That last one is key here, because swapping cards within a deck is basically promos plus. It's one of the few mechanics they haven't toyed with yet.

(Update: trimmed this down a little because, daaaaamn. I got carried away!)

That's a false equivalency. With the exception of promos, which were introduced four years ago back when the game was still young, every single thing you listed was, at least, a deck of its own. New decks or new expansions play with new concepts, and that's great. Maybe one of the new heroes will have cards they can swap in and out of their deck. I don't think they will, but if you want to take that position then I won't argue.

But the fact that because new decks explore new possibility spaces absolutely does not imply that they're just going to start dropping huge new concepts on existing decks. Because half the things you listed are not hugely innovative, or entirely new, and half of the rest have those things as focal points, for decks or even expansions. Something as massive as customising an already existing deck is not going to happen with six cards for a single hero as an afterthought. It just isn't.

posts.name: armadagon
posts.cooked:
PeterCHayward:

Strike Three: Mr. Fixer deals himself up to three damage. Deal X targets 1 damage, where X is the amount of damage Mr. Fixer dealt himself.

 

Wow.  That would make Dual Crowbars insane.  Have Fixer deal himself 3 damage (bumped to 4 thanks to Crowbars), deal 5 damage to a target.  Then deal 2 damage to a target, deal 3 damage to another target, and repeat three more times.  Basically, deal himself 4 damage to spread 25 damage among enemy targets, as long as there are three or more enemies in play.  This would let him easily clear mob-heavy decks like Voss, Matriarch, Dreamer, and Final Wasteland.  Also would make him pretty dominating in Vengeance/Villains style play.  Add a Greased Monkey Fist or other damage boost and he gets even more crazy.  Interestingly, it does not break Jack Handle as much, since he doesn't actually hit himself, so he only gets one shot of damage off; though it does let him deal 3 damage to everything for free, which is still kinda ridiculous.

 

I'm okay with this.
